raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Closes #43133

## Motivation

SRT general plugins are best-effort: a plugin that is missing, filtered out, fails to import, raises in its callback, or has a hook that fails to apply is only logged, and the server starts without it. For a plugin that changes how a model is placed or executed, partial application is worse than none. This implements part 1 of #43133: an opt-in, plugin-agnostic fail-fast. Parts 2 and 3 (read-only hook status, `register(..., required=True)`) are left out; happy to follow up if wanted.

## Modifications

- `environ.py`: add `SGLANG_REQUIRED_PLUGINS = EnvTuple(())` next to `SGLANG_PLUGINS`.
- `plugins/__init__.py`: `load_plugins()` raises a `RuntimeError` naming the plugin and the cause when a listed plugin:
  1. has no entry point in `sglang.srt.plugins`;
  2. is excluded by `SGLANG_PLUGINS` or `SGLANG_PLATFORM`;
  3. raises in `ep.load()`;
  4. raises in its callable;
  5. registered a hook whose target was not applied.

  Load and callable errors are chained (`raise ... from e`), so the original traceback is kept.
- The required set is passed to `load_plugins_by_group()` as a new keyword parameter (default empty), so platform discovery, which shares that function, is unchanged.
- `plugin.mdx`: env-var table row, plus an SRT paragraph in the failure-semantics section.

With the env var unset, behaviour and logs are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A: no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: runs once per process at startup.

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/plugins/test_load_plugins.py`: one test per case (1.1 with and without other plugins installed, 1.2 for both filters, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5), plus two must-not-raise tests (all required present; a failed hook from a non-required plugin). All 7 must-raise tests fail on `main` and pass with this change.

```
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/plugins/ test/registered/unit/platforms/test_platform_interface.py -q
105 passed
```

End to end (CPU, fake entry points, real env var parsing):

| `SGLANG_REQUIRED_PLUGINS` | Result |
|---|---|
| `crashes, bad_hook` | `RuntimeError: Required plugin 'crashes' failed to execute.` (cause: `ValueError('boom')`) |
| `bad_hook` | `RuntimeError: Required plugins could not apply hooks: bad_hook -> sglang.srt.plugins.no_such_function` |
| `missing` | `RuntimeError: Cannot discover required plugins missing.` |
| unset | starts as before |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (N/A, see above)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

nodes.body: @wisclmy0611 @zijiexia @JustinTong0323 @sogalin Could anyone add the CI tag and review the PR? Thanks!
Thanks for the review. I will include part 2 and 3 as part of this PR to close the issue while addressing the feedbacks.

Thanks for picking this up. I filed #43133 for a weight-offloading plugin ([FlexTensor](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/flextensor/issues/6)), and part 1 covers what we need.

I ran f33941f in the `lmsysorg/sglang` nightly dev image (the current head only merges main; this PR's diff is unchanged):
- `test/registered/unit/plugins/` and `test_platform_interface.py`: 105 passed.
- With a minimal plugin shaped like ours (an entry point whose callback registers four hooks on SRT methods) and `SGLANG_REQUIRED_PLUGINS` set, each failure case raises the expected `RuntimeError` from `load_plugins()`, and `python -m sglang.launch_server` exits with it before parsing arguments: plugin not installed, not in `SGLANG_PLUGINS`, import error, raising callback, and a hook on a missing target. With the variable unset, behaviour is unchanged.

Two gaps against case 1.5 are in the inline comments; both reproduce at runtime.

Since parts 2 and 3 are out of scope here, could the description say `Part of #43133` instead of `Closes #43133`, so the issue stays open for them? On your offer to follow up on part 2: yes, please. We would use a read-only hook status. Today our plugin reads `HookRegistry._hooks` / `_patched` to confirm its own hooks were applied.

_Drafted with AI assistance; reviewed and verified by the author._

Hooks registered at import time aren't covered by the final check. `_current_plugin_source` is only set around `func()` in `load_plugins()`, so a required plugin that registers at module scope registers here, during `ep.load()`, with `source=None`. That happens with `@plugin_hook`, or with `HookRegistry.register(...)` at module level as in the "Registration API" section of `plugin.mdx`. The check at the end of `load_plugins()` then skips it (`source is not None and ...`), so a renamed target in such a plugin still starts the server without the hook.

Reproduced on this PR: a required plugin whose `ep.load()` applies `@plugin_hook` to a missing target logs `Failed to apply hooks to ...`, and `load_plugins()` still returns normally.

Setting the context variable around `ep.load()` too would cover it (untested sketch):

```python
            token = _current_plugin_source.set(HookSource(ep.name, dist_name))
            try:
                func = ep.load()
            finally:
                _current_plugin_source.reset(token)
```

A test with a fake entry point whose `load()` applies `@plugin_hook` to a missing target would pin it.

This misses a hook that was registered after its target was already patched. `apply_hooks()` skips any target already in `_patched`. If `apply_hooks()` runs before a required plugin registers, for example because an earlier plugin calls it from its own callback, the required plugin's later hook on the same target is never wrapped. The target is still in `_patched`, though, so nothing is reported. That is the "registered too late" half of case 1.5 in #43133.

Reproduced: when an earlier plugin calls `HookRegistry.apply_hooks()` from its callback and a required plugin then hooks the same target, `load_plugins()` returns normally and the required plugin's hook is never called.

A per-hook comparison would cover it, e.g. recording which `(target, hook)` entries `apply_hooks()` actually wrapped and checking the required plugins' registrations against that.

+        mock_envs.SGLANG_PLUGINS.get.return_value = ""
+        mock_envs.SGLANG_REQUIRED_PLUGINS.get.return_value = ("critical",)
+
+        def bad_fn():
+            raise ValueError("boom!")
+
+        mock_eps.return_value = [_make_ep("critical", load_fn=bad_fn)]
+
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "critical"):
+            load_plugins()
+
+
+def bad_hook_plugin():
+    HookRegistry.register(
+        "sglang.srt.plugins.no_such_function", lambda result, *a, **k: result
+    )
+
+
+class TestLoadPluginsWithRealHookRegistry(CustomTestCase):
+    """Tests for load_plugins() with real `HookRegistry`"""
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        _reset_plugins_loaded()
+        HookRegistry.reset()
+
+    def tearDown(self):
+        _reset_plugins_loaded()
+        HookRegistry.reset()
+
+    @patch("sglang.srt.plugins.envs")
+    @patch("sglang.srt.plugins.entry_points")
+    def test_required_plugins_fail_to_apply(self, mock_eps, mock_envs):
+        """A failed hook from a required plugin raises an exception."""
+        mock_envs.SGLANG_PLATFORM.get.return_value = ""
+        mock_envs.SGLANG_PLUGINS.get.return_value = ""
+        mock_envs.SGLANG_REQUIRED_PLUGINS.get.return_value = ("critical",)
+
+        mock_eps.return_value = [_make_ep("critical", load_fn=bad_hook_plugin)]
+
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "critical.*no_such_function"):
+            load_plugins()
+
+    @patch("sglang.srt.plugins.envs")
+    @patch("sglang.srt.plugins.entry_points")
+    def test_non_required_plugin_fail_to_apply_does_not_raise(
+        self, mock_eps, mock_envs
+    ):
+        """A failed hook from a non-required plugin is only logged."""
+        mock_envs.SGLANG_PLATFORM.get.return_value = ""
+        mock_envs.SGLANG_PLUGINS.get.return_value = ""
+        mock_envs.SGLANG_REQUIRED_PLUGINS.get.return_value = ("critical",)
+
+        mock_eps.return_value = [
+            _make_ep("critical"),
+            _make_ep("trivial", load_fn=bad_hook_plugin),
+        ]
+
+        load_plugins()
+

Hooks registered at import time aren't covered by the final check. `_current_plugin_source` is only set around `func()` in `load_plugins()`, so a required plugin that registers at module scope registers here, during `ep.load()`, with `source=None`. That happens with `@plugin_hook`, or with `HookRegistry.register(...)` at module level as in the "Registration API" section of `plugin.mdx`. The check at the end of `load_plugins()` then skips it (`source is not None and ...`), so a renamed target in such a plugin still starts the server without the hook.

Reproduced on this PR: a required plugin whose `ep.load()` applies `@plugin_hook` to a missing target logs `Failed to apply hooks to ...`, and `load_plugins()` still returns normally.

Setting the context variable around `ep.load()` too would cover it (untested sketch):

```python
            token = _current_plugin_source.set(HookSource(ep.name, dist_name))
            try:
                func = ep.load()
            finally:
                _current_plugin_source.reset(token)
```

A test with a fake entry point whose `load()` applies `@plugin_hook` to a missing target would pin it.

This misses a hook that was registered after its target was already patched. `apply_hooks()` skips any target already in `_patched`. If `apply_hooks()` runs before a required plugin registers, for example because an earlier plugin calls it from its own callback, the required plugin's later hook on the same target is never wrapped. The target is still in `_patched`, though, so nothing is reported. That is the "registered too late" half of case 1.5 in #43133.

Reproduced: when an earlier plugin calls `HookRegistry.apply_hooks()` from its callback and a required plugin then hooks the same target, `load_plugins()` returns normally and the required plugin's hook is never called.

A per-hook comparison would cover it, e.g. recording which `(target, hook)` entries `apply_hooks()` actually wrapped and checking the required plugins' registrations against that.

reviews.body:
Thanks for picking this up. I filed #43133 for a weight-offloading plugin ([FlexTensor](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/flextensor/issues/6)), and part 1 covers what we need.

I ran f33941f in the `lmsysorg/sglang` nightly dev image (the current head only merges main; this PR's diff is unchanged):
- `test/registered/unit/plugins/` and `test_platform_interface.py`: 105 passed.
- With a minimal plugin shaped like ours (an entry point whose callback registers four hooks on SRT methods) and `SGLANG_REQUIRED_PLUGINS` set, each failure case raises the expected `RuntimeError` from `load_plugins()`, and `python -m sglang.launch_server` exits with it before parsing arguments: plugin not installed, not in `SGLANG_PLUGINS`, import error, raising callback, and a hook on a missing target. With the variable unset, behaviour is unchanged.

Two gaps against case 1.5 are in the inline comments; both reproduce at runtime.

Since parts 2 and 3 are out of scope here, could the description say `Part of #43133` instead of `Closes #43133`, so the issue stays open for them? On your offer to follow up on part 2: yes, please. We would use a read-only hook status. Today our plugin reads `HookRegistry._hooks` / `_patched` to confirm its own hooks were applied.
